conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Mr. ___. I'm Dr. ___. You're in the hospital because of shortness of breath. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I smoked some crack a few days ago. Then I started having trouble breathing just walking to the kitchen. It got worse every day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Did you have chest pain or tightness too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, some chest tightness, but it’s better now. I also had a dry cough and felt weak.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. The ambulance team said your blood sugar was low. Do you know why that might have happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t eat much. I’ve been feeling sick. But I take insulin every day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We’ve checked your labs and a chest X-ray. Your lungs show inflammation, likely from the crack use. It’s called cocaine-induced pneumonitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that serious? I’ve been here before for something like this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it can be. Your heart function is already low at 20%, and your lungs are struggling. But we’re going to treat this with steroids and breathing treatments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Steroids? Like for asthma?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Prednisone to reduce lung inflammation. And we’ll give you nebulizers to help open your airways.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. My breathing is a little better since I got oxygen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. You’re on 4 liters now. We’ll try to lower it as you improve. Also, your kidney function was a bit off—creatinine 1.6—but it’s likely due to your heart and not taking your water pill.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I ran out of torsemide two days ago. I didn’t have money for the refill.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve restarted it. It’s important to take it daily to avoid fluid buildup. We’ll help you get it filled after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. What about my diabetes? My sugars have been all over the place.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We started you on 60 units of Lantus in the morning and 50 at night. Steroids can raise blood sugar, so we’ll adjust as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can handle high sugars. I just watch what I eat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That helps, but we still need to keep it under control. We’ll monitor it closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. Still short of breath, but not as bad. Cough’s still there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your oxygen is down to 3 liters. That’s progress. We did an ultrasound on your leg because you had calf tenderness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh yeah, my left leg was sore. Is it a blood clot?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, the ultrasound showed no DVT. The tenderness might be from straining or swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re also watching your kidneys. Your creatinine improved to 1.4 after fluids. That’s a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So my heart and kidneys are both affected?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your heart isn’t pumping well, which can affect your kidneys. That’s why taking your meds daily is so important.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. You’re looking better. Oxygen is at 2 liters now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can walk to the bathroom without stopping. That’s new.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great! The prednisone is helping. We’ll keep you on it for a few more days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it make my sugar worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can, but we’re managing it with higher insulin. Once you finish the steroids, we’ll lower the dose back to 50 twice a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re down to 1 liter of oxygen. Your breathing is much improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel stronger. But I’ve had some diarrhea the last two days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We tested your stool. It’s negative for C. diff and infection. Probably from antibiotics or stress on your system.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it should resolve. Just stay hydrated. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Big news—your oxygen is off! You’re breathing room air and saturating at 94%.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? That’s amazing. I haven’t felt this good in days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The steroids and nebs did their job. Your lung inflammation is calming down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly tomorrow. We want to make sure you’re stable and understand your discharge plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I know I need to take my meds and stop using crack.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the most important thing. You’ve been through this before. This time, let’s try to stay on track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m trying. I’ve got the PACT team helping me, and I have a PET scan coming up for that lung spot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, keep up with that. And weigh yourself every morning. Call if you gain more than 3 pounds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. And take my torsemide every day, even if I feel fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. You’re doing great. Let’s get you ready for discharge tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re cleared to go home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. I feel ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Here’s your discharge plan: continue prednisone until the bottle is empty, then go back to your usual insulin dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. 60 and 50 until the steroids are done, then 50 twice a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. Take all your other meds as prescribed. No skipping torsemide.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. I saw what happens when I stop.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. And please avoid cocaine. It’s damaging your lungs and heart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. I’m going to try to stay clean. I’ve got help lined up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the best thing you can do. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or weight gain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you, doc. I feel like I got a second chance.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did. Make the most of it. Take care.
